newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up, supported by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up, supported by Wall Street.

text.p: French shares held on to their gains to close higher on Wednesday, supported by strength on Wall Street, and traders were moderately hopeful about further progress.
"If New York finishes higher, if the dollar holds steady in around 5.25 francs and rates stay steady, we have the grounds to move a bit higher," said one.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 25.19 points or 1.15 percent at 2,218.89 while the CAC-40 futures settled at 2,221.0 compared with 2,195 on Tuesday.
Technically, the CAC-40 should continue to hover around 2,200 points, analysts said. Analysts said it would be difficult to break through the 2,230/2,240 level and saw major resistance at 2,250.

Axa climbed 1.54 percent to 309.50 francs following the expiry of its paper offer for UAP. The companies announced a new executive lineup for the merged group that bore Axa's stamp. Ten of the 16 members of the executive committee hail from Axa. "It's a good thing, Axa knows how to run things," said one analyst, commenting on the structure.

* Catering group Sodexho adds 3.19 percent to 2,619 francs after reporting 1995/96 pre-exceptional profit up 41 percent and forecasting 25 percent rise in pre-exceptional profits for 1996/1997. Company chairman Pierre Bellon bullish on future, hoping for "good sales and profit growth in the coming years".
* SBC Warburg downgrades Club Med, off 3.79 percent to 340.50 francs, telling clients to lighten holdings.

* Shares in luxury goods group LVMH soars 8.37 percent at 1,375 francs after arbitrator clears bid to buy U.S. duty free chain DFS. LVMH forecasts deal will boost operating profits by some 30 percent. The decision resolves a quarrel among DFS shareholders over the deal but it still needs U.S. anti-trust clearance. "The fact the arbitrator has given approval removes uncertainty," a trader said.
* Bank Credit National climbs 7.5 percent on press report speculating it could be bid target, saying its share price was undervalued. But analysts uncertain who would bid.
